name: Negative Pull-Up
equipmentItems: Stable bench or step for setup
grip: Overhand pronated grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
description: Start at the top position with chin over the bar and lower your body in a slow, controlled eccentric descent to a full dead hang, overloading eccentric latissimus strength to build pull-up capacity.
setup: Place a sturdy bench or box directly underneath a pull-up bar.
Step onto the box and grasp the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width.
Jump or step up to bring your chin cleared over the bar with chest lifted and shoulders depressed.
instructions: Take your feet off the box, bracing your core and holding the top position momentarily.
Lower your body in a deliberate, uniform descent lasting 3 to 5 seconds.
Control the entire range of motion, actively resisting gravity with your lats and arm flexors.
Continue lowering until your arms are fully extended in a dead hang at the bottom.
Step back onto the box to reset for the next repetition.
cues: Count 3 to 5 seconds on the way down.
Keep shoulders controlled, don't drop suddenly.
Lower all the way to straight arms.
commonMistakes: Free-falling or letting go in the bottom third of the descent.
Kicking the legs or swinging violently during the descent.
Failing to reach full dead-hang extension before resetting.

logging.example: 5 repetitions with 5-second descent: record 5 reps (note 5s eccentric).
logging.note: Record repetitions and target eccentric duration per repetition (typically 3–5 seconds).

variantNote: Eccentric-only pull-up protocol utilizing supra-maximal eccentric loading to develop neuromuscular lat recruitment and concentric pull-up capability.
reviewNotes: Panel A shows top chin-over-bar position; panel B shows controlled lowering to full dead hang.
